exposure: intrathecal hyperbaric bupivacaine 4.5mg with volume extension technique (EVE 10ml normal saline)
intrathecal hyperbaric bupivacaine 5.5mg with volume extension technique (EVE 10ml normal saline)
intrathecal hyperbaric bupivacaine 6mg with volume extension technique (EVE 10ml normal saline)
outcome: maternal hemodynamic variables (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean blood pressure, heart rate)
cohort: 145 parturient women with ASA I-II physical status undergoing elective cesarean section were divided into three groups based on the bupivacaine dose received.
finding: The combined spinal-epidural anesthesia with volume extension technique using 4.5mg intrathecal hyperbaric bupivacaine resulted in significantly lower maternal hemodynamic instability and hypotension compared to 5.5mg and 6mg doses during elective cesarean sections.
